subject: Deferred prefetch + variant fallback: coordination and mitigation
messages:
From: Simon Clark <simon.clark@northway.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@northway.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Nov 2028 15:13:00 -0700
Subject: Quick sync: intermittent latency spikes + prefetch behavior

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Northway's ingestion pipeline is moving fast and we want to finish the final integration test this week. During our smoke runs we see periodic 200–800ms latency spikes on generation calls that are correlated with long warm-up traces. The engineer attached a short trace (prefetch-trace-20281101.json) — it looks like the SDK is falling back to a variant that has a different KV cache warm path.

This matters because our UI times out after ~700ms for the live editor. Can Redwood share any guidance to avoid the fallback (or a mitigation we can ship) so we don't get unexpected regressions in production?

Appreciate a quick triage — we have a slot with Procurement next Thursday.

— Simon
Customer Success / Northway AI
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Simon Clark <simon.clark@northway.ai>, Priya Rao <priya@northway.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Nov 2028 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Quick sync: intermittent latency spikes + prefetch behavior

Team — forwarding a Northway report. TL;DR: SDK-triggered fallback to a variant/route is causing KV-cache warm-up and intermittent +500ms spikes. Customer hits UI timeout. They need a short-term mitigation and a longer-term fix.

Ask: can Platform/Runtime confirm whether:
- SDK prefetch is sometimes routed to a smaller-memory variant (causes cache miss walk)
- any mitigation knobs exist to pin variant or force a warmed prefix on request path

I can jump into a quick call with Simon/Priya if helpful. Priority: high for this account (Procurement next Thu).

Thanks — Logan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Simon Clark <simon.clark@northway.ai>, Priya Rao <priya@northway.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Nov 2028 08:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick sync: intermittent latency spikes + prefetch behavior

Thanks for the ping and the trace, Logan / Simon. I dug into the trace you attached. Quick summary: the request flow shows an initial prefetch request hitting the routing plane where a capacity-optimized variant (quantized) was selected under burst conditions. That variant's optimized path avoids some big-kernel warm paths on steady state but does not share the same KV cache packing strategy, so the first live generation after a prefetch pays a penalty when the cache is reconstructed.

Short-term mitigations we can offer:
- SDK flag to set "variant_preference=prefer_stable" (forces routing to variants that share KV packing) — we can gate this per-API-key.
- Add a optional "prefetch_warm=true" header the SDK can send; runtime will perform a cheap KV-touch to align caches (adds ~20–40ms to the prefetch call but avoids large warm-ups later).

Longer-term: we should make the routing decision respect an incoming prefetch intent header so prefetches are always pinned to cache-compatible variants; that's a small change in router + runtime. I can PR an initial patch for the header behavior.

Questions for Sales Engs: would you prefer the SDK flag (fast to ship) or the prefetch_warm header (safer for end-user latency)?

I'll coordinate a dev branch and a canary route if we decide to implement.

— Karthik
Principal Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Simon Clark <simon.clark@northway.ai>, Priya Rao <priya@northway.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Nov 2028 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick sync: intermittent latency spikes + prefetch behavior

Appreciate the clear analysis, Karthik. For Northway: they want minimal user-facing latency and are sensitive to any change that increases prefetch cost. My recommendation (from Sales Eng perspective): ship the SDK flag first (so customers can opt-in per key) and iterate the prefetch_warm header as a productized default for our managed customers.

Action items:
- Platform: can you scope the SDK flag (API surface, validation) + a runtime gate for "prefer_stable" routing? Estimate: small config + router check — please confirm ETA.
- Dev/QA: we need a canary run against NW account to reproduce the pattern. Simon, we'll coordinate a short window Tuesday morning.
- Sales: I'll prepare a short note for Procurement to explain mitigation.

Ping Marissa for pricing/commit questions if variant pinning changes pricing bands.

— Logan
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Simon Clark <simon.clark@northway.ai>, Priya Rao <priya@northway.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Nov 2028 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick sync: intermittent latency spikes + prefetch behavior

Looping back with a quick implementation note. Karthik and I sketched the change:
- SDK: add optional enum prefetchVariantPreference {any, prefer_stable} default=any. Validation server-side will accept the header X-RW-Prefetch-Variant: stable when enabled for API key. Deliverable: SDK patch + compatibility docs in 2 business days.
- Runtime: router accepts the header and will match against a new label on variants (stable=true). No config reload required; small cost to route. Canary rollout targeted for next Wed.
- Telemetry: we'll emit a metric prefetch.variant_pin and first_gen.kv_warm_time so we can measure effectiveness. JIRA: RINF-8432 created.

I can prep the SDK PR today and open the runtime change as an RFC. If Sales wants the prefetch_warm header as an alternative, we can prototype it after the SDK flag lands.

I'll schedule a 30-min call with Simon for Tuesday 09:00 PT for the canary run.

— Dev Patel
Software Engineer, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
